title: Evaluating AI’s Coding Ability Beyond Benchmarks
description:
This is a teaser for Adam Larson’s full session at AI Native DevCon Fall, November 18–19.

Benchmarks often claim a model is “best at coding,” but anyone building with LLMs knows leaderboard metrics don’t always translate to real-world results. Some models ace synthetic tests yet struggle in production. Why? And how do we measure what actually matters?

In this preview, Adam Larson (Founder & CTO, Raleon) shares how he thinks about evaluating LLMs for real software development, the testing systems he's building, and where current benchmarks fall short.

In the full DevCon talk, you will learn:
- Key dimensions that define an LLM’s coding ability
- Why benchmark scores ≠ real-world performance
- How to evaluate models in practical developer workflows
- Approaches to test and stress-test AI coding assistants
- The future of trustworthy evaluation for AI-augmented engineering

If you’re serious about deploying AI into real engineering environments — not demo-land — this session is essential.

Speaker
Adam Larson — Founder & CTO, Raleon
20 years in software engineering
Game industry alum (Batman Arkham Asylum, BurgerTime)
Former Director of Engineering Analytics at nCino (IPO)
Now building AI-driven D2C technology at Raleon
